metadata.summary: An age-old rivalry will bookend the Rugby League World Cup 2026 in the latest symbol that rugby league worldwide has grown but, ultimately, the contenders are still just contenders and the favourites remain just that.
metadata.content: Australia vs New Zealand: Age-old rivalry bookends Rugby League World Cup but will it end 18 years of supremacy? | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Opinion Australia vs New Zealand: Age-old rivalry bookends Rugby League World Cup but will it end 18 years of supremacy? In the men's and women's Rugby League World Cup finals Australia will take on New Zealand; the last time both New Zealand teams won the tournament was back in 2008, nearly two decades ago; the finals take place on Sunday November 16 Megan Wellens Sports Journalist @MegWellensX Monday 9 November 2026 11:25, UK Image: New Zealand are looking to lift the Rugby League World Cup for the first time since 2008 An age-old rivalry will bookend the Rugby League World Cup 2026 in the latest symbol that rugby league worldwide has grown but, ultimately, the contenders are still just contenders and the favourites remain just that. In a sensational opener to the tournament, Australia clinched a dramatic 24-22 victory over New Zealand in front of the biggest Test crowd in 50 years, surpassing the previous benchmark set in 1974. Now, the two men's teams will meet once again to decide who will be world champions. And in the women's tournament, the same showdown will decide who is on top. metadata.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins has called a press conference for Friday to have his say on 'Sandpapergate' after former team-mate Usman Khawaja's explosive claims that the entire dressing room knew about the ball-tampering scheme that took place on the tour of South Africa in 2018.

Australia captain Pat Cummins has called a press conference for Friday to have his say on 'Sandpapergate' after former team-mate Usman Khawaja's explosive claims that the entire dressing room knew about the ball-tampering scheme that took place on the tour of South Africa in 2018. Khawaja made the revelations in his new book 'Sabr', bringing the scandal back onto the agenda after eight years. Cummins has been rested for the white-ball series' against England, which also begins on Friday with the first ODI in Perth, but has publicly invited a media grilling in Sydney for that same morning. messages.text: Why have Man Utd only had two 'successful' managers?

metadata.content: Why have Man Utd only had two 'successful' managers? | Football News | Sky Sports MU Skip to main content Skip to main content By William Bitibiri Only three managers have won the league with Manchester United. Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt knew two. Ernest Mangnall was the name that stopped them. “Who!?” “Never heard of him,” Butt said. Scholes was equally puzzled. Mangnall won United’s first two league titles, in 1907-08 and 1910-11. Sir Matt Busby added five, Sir Alex Ferguson 13. “F****** hell,” Scholes replied. Titles at Man Utd 20 League titles 3 Title-winning managers 18 Titles won by Sir Alex Ferguson and Sir Matt Busby It is an understandable reaction. More than a century on, Mangnall’s achievements have faded from the conversation around United’s greatest managers. His two titles are often overlooked beside the five won by Busby and the 13 delivered by Ferguson. But the numbers tell an unusual story. United have won 20 league titles under just three managers. Liverpool have also won 20, but theirs have been shared between six: Bill Shankly, Bob Paisley, Joe Fagan, Kenny Dalglish, Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot. Busby and Ferguson account for 18 of United’s 20. Their influence went beyond trophies. They shaped teams, set standards and helped define the club’s identity. That raises a question beyond the familiar search for Ferguson’s successor.
